title: The Beginners of a Nation A History of the Source and Rise of the Earliest English Settlements in America, with Special Reference to the Life and Character of the People

This work delves into the origins and development of the earliest English settlements in America, examining the social, political, intellectual, and religious contexts that motivated emigration from England. Eggleston aims to portray the colonists not as revered forefathers but as ordinary people possessing both virtues and flaws. He highlights the dire conditions faced by the first settlers, their struggles for survival, and the challenges posed by both the harsh new environment and interactions with Indigenous populations.
